subject: Quantium Retail POC activation & escalation plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@quantiumretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-10T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Quantium Retail POC activation - recap and next steps

Hi Aisha / Samir —

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps to get the POC turned on next week. Please confirm these items and the timeline below so we can lock resources.

Recap (as we heard it)
- Goal: Validate 95th-percentile latency < 300ms for retrieval-augmented generation across 3 product flows and confirm cost per 1k tokens for our baseline model.
- Success criteria: throughput target (200 qps sustained), response quality (BLEU-style relevance > 0.78 on your eval set), and SLO guardrails for cold-starts.
- Scope: 2 model endpoints (low-latency variant, cost-optimized variant), sample dataset (~50k rows), integration with your staging S3, and SSO access for 4 reviewers.

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline
- Wed 2027-04-14: preflight checklist & credentials exchanged (point of contact: Samir)
- Thu 2027-04-15: dry-run ingest + smoke tests (owner: Redwood infra / Vivek)
- Mon 2027-04-19: canary run (10% traffic) across one product flow (owner: Quantium + Redwood)
- Tue 2027-04-20: full acceptance window opens (3 business days) with daily metric syncs

Owners & actions (who does what)
- Quantium: provide staging S3 credentials, procurement PO or procurement contact confirmation (Aisha / Samir)
- Redwood: deliver runbook + evaluation matrix (attached), provide on-call engineer during dry-run (Vivek)

Immediate asks for you
1) Confirm procurement contact and target PO date (we need a PO or SOW approval to reserve dedicated capacity).
2) Confirm sampling dataset link and a primary reviewer for each product flow.
3) Approve the attached runbook & evaluation-matrix, or flag edits by EOD Tue 2027-04-12.

Attachments: quantium_poc-runbook.pdf, evaluation-matrix.xlsx, redwood-sow-draft.pdf

If this looks good I will schedule the dry-run with Vivek and put the canary on the calendar.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Quantium preflight & risk call follow-up

Quick internal note after Marissa’s recap — we should call out likely blockers and assign mitigations before the dry-run:

Potential blockers we may see:
- Network egress / firewall rules from Quantium staging causing blocked artifact pulls (ftp/s3 endpoints).
- SSO and role mapping delays for the 4 reviewers (could delay acceptance testing).
- Large sequence-length distribution from their eval set (they mentioned long product descriptions). This can expose memory pressure on our default runtime.
- Procurement timing (Aisha expects PO by 4/16; we need an SOW to speed this).

Suggested mitigations + owners:
- Preflight: ask Quantium for a test account + sample manifest; infra to validate S3 access (owner: Vivek).
- SSO: coordinate with Evelyn to provide short-lived access tokens and a step-by-step for reviewers.
- Sequence length: engineering to run a quick profiling pass on a 10k-sample to check sequence distribution and estimate token counts. If median seq > 1024, recommend using cost-optimized quantized variant and a smaller batch size.
- Procurement: Marissa to send SOW draft and pricing band.

Vivek — can you confirm ETA for profiling and whether you need anything from Quantium to do it? If there are infra-level issues (OOMs), we may need an urgent patch or a temporary config change.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-13T16:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Quantium preflight & risk call follow-up

Ben / team — quick update from profiling run against the 10k sample that Aisha agreed to share (thanks, Aisha). Summary below:

Findings:
1) Sequence-length distribution: median ~ 720 tokens, 95th percentile ~ 2,900 tokens.
2) When using the low-latency model with default batch_size=8 and kv-cache active, we see intermittent OOMs on the serving nodes for sequences > 2048. Root cause appears to be a kv cache allocation edge case combined with CUDA allocation fragmentation in our current runtime build.

Immediate mitigations (short-term):
- For the dry-run/canary: switch the low-latency endpoint to the cost-optimized (quantized) variant which reduces memory footprint ~35% and avoids the kv-cache path that triggers the bug. (ETA: immediate; config change only.)
- Reduce batch_size to 2 for requests that exceed 2k tokens and enable token streaming to limit peak memory.
- Provide a lightweight preprocessor to truncate/pad the top 5% of sequences if customer accepts minimal loss in QA.

Longer-term fix:
- Engineering will patch the kv-cache allocator and push a runtime build that fixes the fragmentation behavior. I’ve opened JIRA SUP-3421 for the estimator and attached a minimal repro. Estimated fix + QA: 48 hours (targeting 2027-04-15T18:00:00-07:00).

Attachments referenced: diagnostic-log.txt (small repro trace)

If we agree on the short-term mitigations I can flip the endpoint config before the dry-run. We should also document this as a POC risk and include the canary rollback plan.

— Vivek
Staff Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@quantiumretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Quantium Retail (procurement) <procurement@quantiumretail.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quantium Retail POC activation - recap and next steps (mitigation & escalation plan)

Hi Aisha / Samir —

Following internal profiling, we discovered a potential runtime OOM for very long sequences. We do not expect this to block the dry-run if we implement the mitigations below; here’s our proposal and escalation path so you have visibility.

Proposed short-term mitigations (to proceed with canary 4/19 as planned)
- Redwood will flip the low-latency endpoint to the quantized (cost-optimized) variant for the canary. This reduces memory and keeps latency in an acceptable range. (Action: Vivek — done before dry-run.)
- We will apply request-level throttling: batch_size=2 for requests >2000 tokens and enable streaming.
- If any job hits the OOM threshold during the canary we will immediately divert that request to the cost-optimized endpoint and log the event.

Canary acceptance / go-no-go criteria
- No more than 1% request failures attributed to memory issues across the canary window.
- Latency P95 < 400ms (with quantized variant).
- Quality regression (as measured by your eval metrics) < 4% vs baseline.

Escalation path (if short-term mitigation fails)
1) On OOM events, engineering (Vivek) will triage and apply the config rollback. JIRA SUP-3421 will be the reference ticket.
2) If root cause appears in runtime build, Redwood will provide a dedicated hotfix branch and a patch ETA inside SUP-3421.
3) If mitigation cannot be achieved within 24 hours and the canary cannot proceed, Redwood proposes pausing and re-scheduling the canary for the next available window (we’ll coordinate with procurement on new dates).

Next steps (today)
- Marissa: Share 1-page SOW and updated runbook (attached) — sending now (redwood-sow-draft.pdf).
- Aisha: Confirm if procurement can accept a SOW + redwood invoice template for PO routing.
- Vivek: Flip endpoint config to quantized variant and confirm once complete.
- Evelyn: Prepare step-by-step SSO / reviewer access notes and send to Priya/Jorge.

Please reply with a single-line approval to proceed with the mitigations & canary or tell us if you prefer to pause until the runtime patch is merged.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
